title: From emotional signal to useful next step

purpose.objective: Practice one short, voluntary emotion-regulation step without suppressing feelings or judging personal worth.
purpose.meaning: Make it easier to understand an emotional signal and choose a safe action aligned with personal values.

options.title: Ground attention
options.description: Notice the surroundings, relax the body where comfortable, and let the first wave settle.

options.title: Separate fact from interpretation
options.description: Write one observable fact, one interpretation, and one thing that remains unknown.

options.title: Choose one useful action
options.description: Identify one small, safe action that addresses a solvable part of the situation.

options.title: Connect or communicate
options.description: Consider asking a trusted person a question, requesting support, or stating a respectful boundary.

options.title: Pause and recover
options.description: Choose rest, reduce the demand, or postpone the decision when that is the most appropriate response.

steps.instruction: Choose one option, adapt it, or decline the quest. No emotional disclosure is required.
Try the selected response for a few minutes. Do not force a positive interpretation or ignore a real safety concern.
Optionally note whether the response was useful, neutral, or unhelpful. You do not need to record your emotion or share personal details.

success_criteria: One response was freely chosen, adapted, or the quest was declined.
The response respected real-world safety and personal boundaries.
No positive mood, emotional suppression, personal score, streak, or public disclosure was required.

deliverables.description: No personal reflection or emotional data needs to be stored or shared.

feedback.method: Offer a neutral reflection on the chosen strategy and one optional next step. Never infer a diagnosis or claim that the person's mood improved.

rewards.description: No reward is necessary; the value is the optional practice and the choice remains with the participant.
